papers.title: In vitro meat: A future animal-free harvest.
papers.abstract: In vitro meat production is a novel idea of producing meat without involving animals with the help of tissue engineering techniques. This biofabrication of complex living products by using various bioengineering techniques is a potential solution to reduce the ill effects of current meat production systems and can dramatically transform traditional animal-based agriculture by inventing "animal-free" meat and meat products. Nutrition-related diseases, food-borne illnesses, resource use and pollution, and use of farm animals are some serious consequences associated with conventional meat production methods. This new way of animal-free meat production may offer health and environmental advantages by reducing environmental pollution and resource use associated with current meat production systems and will also ensure sustainable production of designer, chemically safe, and disease-free meat as the conditions in an in vitro meat production system are controllable and manipulatable. Theoretically, this system is believed to be efficient enough to supply the global demand for meat; however, establishment of a sustainable in vitro meat production would face considerably greater technical challenges and a great deal of research is still needed to establish this animal-free meat culturing system on an industrial scale.

llm.relevance_to_user: 这篇论文讨论了基于组织工程的体外肉生产，但完全没有涉及人工智能或生物打印技术，与研究者的AI生物打印方向不相关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a general review on in vitro meat production using tissue engineering, with no incorporation of AI into bioprinting workflow stages, no experimental validation of a bioprinting process, and no discussion of autonomous decision-making.

summary_zh.motivation: 传统肉类生产带来环境和健康问题，体外肉生产作为替代方案。
summary_zh.method: 利用组织工程技术进行动物肉类的体外培养。
summary_zh.result: 理论上可满足全球肉类需求，但工业化仍面临技术挑战。
summary_zh.validation: 无实验验证，仅为理论综述。

summary_en.motivation: Conventional meat production causes environmental and health issues, motivating the development of in vitro meat as a sustainable alternative.
summary_en.method: The paper reviews the use of tissue engineering techniques to produce meat without animal slaughter.
summary_en.result: In vitro meat production is theoretically feasible to meet global demand, but significant technical hurdles remain for industrial-scale implementation.
summary_en.validation: No experimental validation is presented; the paper is a conceptual review.
